back: The quantity of a good or service that producers are willing and able to offer for sale at each price over a given period of time.
Other things being equal, as price rises quantity supplied rises, and as price falls quantity supplied falls.

front: How does a normal supply curve slope?
back: Upwards from left to right (a direct relationship between price and quantity supplied).

front: Give three reasons why supply rises with price.
back: Higher profit per unit; a higher price covers the rising cost of extra output; new producers enter.
A rise in quantity supplied caused by a rise in the good's own price: a movement up along the supply curve.
A fall in quantity supplied caused by a fall in the good's own price: a movement down along the supply curve.
Add the quantities supplied by all producers at each price.

front: Does a change in a good's own price shift its supply curve?
back: No. It causes a movement along the curve; only non-price factors shift it.
